@graph.summary: The review step of an incremental FHIR IG build, as its own subprocess: list and inspect the differences between the incremental IG AST and what a full build would have produced, then accept them or raise a finding.
@graph.description:
The review step of an incremental FHIR IG build, as its own subprocess: list and inspect the differences between the incremental IG AST and what a full build would have produced, then accept them or raise a finding. THE REVIEW STEP OF AN INCREMENTAL IG BUILD, drawn as its own subprocess (bean `a9tx`, owner 2026-09-30: "list and view differentials/deltas against AST ... as part of (sub-?)process/skills/tools, including pipeline rendering").

WHERE IT SITS. In `ig-incremental-build.bpmn` it belongs between Task_Merge and Task_Qa: after the restored and rebuilt records are merged, before the QC gates read the aggregate. That diagram predates the AST work and is not edited here; `ig-ast-delta` §"Where this sits in a process" states the placement until it is.

WHAT IT GUARDS. An incremental build rebuilds only the cone of a change, computed on the BASE edges. If the cone rules miss a coupling, a resource that should have changed does not, and nothing downstream can tell: the merged AST looks exactly like a correct one. So a person reads the delta, and a difference nobody can explain is treated as a missed coupling rather than as a curiosity.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM. A clean review says the delta is explained, not that the IG is correct. The AST stays a cache: every rendered page carries the provisional mark, and a release is still cut from a full build (`ig-publisher-reduction` P4).

An IG site, built from the AST on its cache branch
@graph.summary: How an IG repository's own site is published, and how the AST it is built from is kept current (skill `ig-build-pipeline` §"The AST cache lifecycle").
@graph.description:
How an IG repository's own site is published, and how the AST it is built from is kept current (skill `ig-build-pipeline` §"The AST cache lifecycle"). Owner, 2026-10-14: "i want AST to be used. it should be in cache branch", and "that should be in fhir-harness then smart-* all use that".

THE RULE. An IG site is built from the IG Publisher AST read from the IG repository's cache branch `cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>`, never from Publisher HTML. The publish refuses an AST that is not valid for the commit it publishes (`ig-cache.sh restore` then `verify`). A later commit that changes no IG input (`sushi-config.yaml`, `ig.ini`, `input/`) does not make the AST stale.

THE REFRESH. The cache is written by ONE thing: fhir-harness's reusable workflow `.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml`, which an IG repository's Site publish calls as its first job (`ast`; template `templates/ig-repo-site/site-publish.yml`). It runs the Publisher through the AST exporter on a GitHub runner (Java, a 10 GB heap, tx.fhir.org), because an agent's container cannot. It seeds the branch only from a commit on the default branch whose inputs equal the tip's.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM. A valid AST is a cache built from these inputs; it is not a release. Every page drawn from it carries the provisional mark (`ig-ast-delta`).

Written by `bun run cat node-kinds`, which only shrinks it; `--accept-unkinded` grows it deliberately.

@graph.name: build-ig-site
@graph.title: Stage one IG as its own just-the-docs Jekyll site
@graph.description: Turn an IG source repository into ONE Jekyll source for just-the-docs, as the IG Publisher builds one IG per site: `input/pagecontent` pages with title, parent and order from `sushi-config.yaml` `pages:`, the files the Publisher's include tags resolve against, images, `_data/fhir.json` from `ig-site-data`, and a `_config.yml`. The pages render unchanged, including their references to the IG's site data (bean `bamf`, owner's choice of one site per IG). With the IG's menu, the layout is the one every IG site wears (bean `mftp`): the IG's own top bar, the IG's TOC declared as the folio-assistant navbar's section (added by `rail-standalone-pages`), no sidebar of its own, an edit link per page, and per heading a source-line link and a pre-filled feedback issue.

inputs.name: ig-src
inputs.description: The IG source repository: `sushi-config.yaml` and `input/`.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: The Jekyll source directory to write.

inputs.name: baseurl
inputs.description: Where the built site is served.

inputs.name: plantuml-jar
inputs.description: Render `input/images-source/*.plantuml` as the Publisher does; without it a visible `not rendered` marker stands in.

outputs.name: pages
outputs.description: Pages staged.

outputs.name: not-rendered
outputs.description: Included files the source does not hold and nothing rendered, each replaced by a VISIBLE marker and listed, never an empty include.

@graph.name: check-wireframe-questionnaire
@graph.title: Check a Questionnaire field for field against the wireframe it was derived from
@graph.description: Compare the `data-element` fields of a mid-fidelity wireframe (per `data-layout`, in document order) with the answerable items of a BUILT Questionnaire (depth first, named by `definition` or `code`). Reports a field with no item, an item with no field, an item naming no data element, a data element twice in one layout, and the first place the order differs. Fidelity, not design. Moved down from the WHO layer on the owner's ruling of 2026-10-14: nothing in it is WHO's.

inputs.name: wireframe
inputs.description: The wireframe HTML; fields carry `data-element`, layouts `data-layout`.

inputs.name: questionnaire
inputs.description: The built Questionnaire JSON (`fsh-generated/resources/Questionnaire-<id>.json`), never FSH.

outputs.name: findings
outputs.description: One line per finding, prefixed with its layout. Exit 0 faithful, 1 a finding, 2 an input could not be read (never a pass).

@graph.name: fhir-cache-seed-npm
@graph.title: Seed the FHIR package cache from trusted sources (exact versions)
@graph.description: Fill `~/.fhir/packages` (or `--cache`) for an environment that cannot reach packages.fhir.org, from trust anchors only: npm account `grahamegrieve` (owner-trusted), publishers' own published-site repositories (the seeder's list, each fetch verified against the tarball's own package.json), template repos found through FHIR/ig-registry's templates.json read live each run, and an owner `--mirror`. Exact versions only (a patch wildcard resolves as the Publisher resolves it, recorded); every tarball verified; nothing computed once and kept; provenance recorded; missing versions listed, never substituted.

inputs.name: sushi-config
inputs.description: Seed what this IG pins: its `dependencies:` and the core package for its `fhirVersion`.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: Default `~/.fhir/packages`, which SUSHI and the IG Publisher read.

inputs.name: dry-run
inputs.description: Resolve and report; download nothing.

inputs.name: mirror
inputs.description: A directory or git repository of `<name>#<version>.tgz` filled by `fhir-package-mirror`.

inputs.name: missing-out
inputs.description: Write the missing list, one `name#version` per line: the input `fhir-package-mirror` takes.

outputs.name: missing
outputs.description: Exit 1 when any is missing. Each is listed with why: not on npm, a different version only, an untrusted maintainer, or not an exact version.

@graph.name: fhir-package-mirror
@graph.title: Mirror FHIR packages from packages.fhir.org into a git repository
@graph.description: On a machine that reaches packages.fhir.org, fetch exactly a missing list (from `fhir-cache-seed-npm --missing-out`), check each tarball names itself exactly, record SHA512SUMS, and commit and push to a git repository that an environment without packages.fhir.org reads with `--mirror`. The person running it is the trust anchor for what it adds.

inputs.name: mirror-repo-dir
inputs.description: A git checkout to fill; committed and pushed when it is one.

inputs.name: missing
inputs.description: The seeder's `--missing-out` file, so nothing unneeded is mirrored.

outputs.name: mirrored
outputs.description: Exit non-zero when any could not be fetched or named itself differently.

@graph.name: fsh-cone
@graph.title: FSH dependency cone
@graph.description: Compute the dependency cone over an IG's FSH graph, and the blast radius of a set of changed files. What makes an incremental IG build possible: without it, any edit rebuilds everything.

inputs.name: igRoot
inputs.description: The IG root holding the FSH sources. Absent, the command exits 2 with its usage — could-not-determine, not an empty cone.

inputs.name: csv
inputs.description: Write the report as CSV to this path instead of printing it.

inputs.name: top
inputs.description: Show only the N largest cones. `0` is a legitimate request for none, which is why `Count` admits zero.

inputs.name: history
inputs.description: Report the blast radius over the last N commits instead of a static cone.

inputs.name: fileUsers
inputs.description: Also write `fsh-file-users/v1`: for each FSH file, the files that use what it declares. The IG AST's incremental plan reads it (`AstPlanCli -fsh-users`) so a changed RuleSet- or Alias-only file reaches its users rather than forcing a full build (bean `a9tx`).

outputs.name: cone
outputs.description: The cone, or the impact of `--changed`. With `--csv` it goes to that path instead.

@graph.name: ig-artifact-jsonld
@graph.title: Write one JSON-LD node per IG artefact, and check a built site's nodes
@graph.description: `write` turns an artefact index into `artifact/<Type>-<id>.jsonld` (and a `.json` twin) under a docs root: one `folio-ig-artifact-jsonld/v1` node per artefact, in borrowed vocabularies only (the FHIR RDF class, dcterms, schema.org, PROV), naming the artefact's canonical URL, its representations and, for a compiled copy, what built it. `check` is the kind's QA: over a BUILT site, every artefact has its node and no node is an orphan, each node is its own file's, its twin matches, and every local resource it names is on the site. It also writes and checks the index node, `artifact/index.jsonld` (`folio-ig-artifact-index-jsonld/v1`): every artefact once, each entry naming its node. WHO-free; the assets the thin pages render (owner, 2026-10-11, option A; thin by default since 2026-10-12).

inputs.name: command
inputs.description: `write` or `check`.

inputs.name: index
inputs.description: The `folio-fhir-artifact-index/v2` to write from, or to check against.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: `write`: the docs root the nodes go under.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: `check`: the built docs root to check.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: `write`: the docs root's published URL, for absolute IRIs.

inputs.name: compiled-data
inputs.description: `write`: where compiled resource files are served, from the docs root.

outputs.name: nodes
outputs.description: Nodes written, or checked; `check` exits 1 with each finding named.

@graph.name: ig-ast-diff
@graph.title: List and view the delta between two IG ASTs
@graph.description: Diff two ASTs by resource key: added, removed, changed (with a structural element-level differential) and version-changed resources, plus edges added and removed; optionally fold in the incremental plan, and render just-the-docs pages (an index that lists, a page per resource that shows) every one of which carries the provisional mark. `list <ast>` summarises one AST.

invoke.shell: bun run fhir-harness/scripts/ig-ast.ts diff <base> <head> [--plan plan.json] [--json delta.json] [--site <dir>]

inputs.name: site
inputs.description: A directory inside the IG's just-the-docs source; pages are wrapped in Liquid raw blocks so FHIR narratives' Liquid is not executed.

outputs.name: pages
outputs.description: Pages written: one index, one per changed or version-changed resource.

@graph.name: ig-ast-export
@graph.title: Build an IG and write its AST
@graph.description: Run one ordinary IG Publisher build through `AstPublisher` (a subclass that overrides nothing) and write the AST beside `output/`: one JSON file per resource keyed `canonical|version`, `dependencies.json` (upstream's DependencyAnalyser plus the Library/PlanDefinition/ActivityDefinition/Measure edges it leaves empty), SUSHI's `fsh-index.json`, and a manifest that declares itself a cache and records the inputs it is valid for.

install.cli: git clone -b claude/ast-export https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher && cd fhir-ig-publisher/ast-export && mvn -q package && mvn -q dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile=cp.txt

inputs.name: ig
inputs.description: The IG root.

inputs.name: ast-out
inputs.description: Default `<ig>/output-ast`, OUTSIDE the Publisher's `output/`.

outputs.name: resources
outputs.description: Resources written, one file each.

outputs.name: edges
outputs.description: Dependency edges, including those whose target is outside the IG (kept, `resolved: null`).

@graph.name: ig-ast-incremental-build
@graph.title: Rebuild only the cone of a change and merge it into the AST
@graph.description: Write the unchanged part of a base AST as a FHIR package into the package cache, build a temporary IG of only the rebuild set with the stock Publisher, merge the result into a mixed-provenance AST (`builtAt` per resource), and repeat while the merged graph's cone reaches resources that were not rebuilt.

install.cli: git clone -b claude/ast-export https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher && cd fhir-ig-publisher/ast-export && mvn -q package && mvn -q dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile=cp.txt

inputs.name: cache-folder
inputs.description: Keeps the `*.ast-cache` packages out of `~/.fhir/packages`.

inputs.name: fsh-users
inputs.description: `fsh-file-users/v1` from `fsh-cone --file-users`, so a changed RuleSet- or Alias-only file reaches its users instead of forcing a full build.

outputs.name: rounds
outputs.description: Rounds to a fixed point; exit 3 when it does not converge, which means run a full build.

@graph.name: ig-ast-jsonld
@graph.title: Export an IG AST as JSON-LD
@graph.description: Write an AST as linked data against `fhir-harness/schemas/ig-ast.context.jsonld`: each resource a node identified by its canonical URL (`urn:fhir:<Type>/<id>` when it has none) and typed by its FHIR resource type, each dependency edge a link to its target, and the manifest's `authority: cache` and `provisional` list carried on the graph. The AST is validated against the Zod declaration the JSON Schemas are generated from before it is exported (bean `l0lq`).

outputs.name: jsonld
outputs.description: JSON-LD on stdout.

@graph.name: ig-ast-list
@graph.title: Summarise one IG AST
@graph.description: Counts per resource type, edges in total and resolved inside the IG, edges by origin (upstream's DependencyAnalyser or ast-export's LogicEdges), whether the AST is mixed-provenance and how many resources each revision built, and what the manifest declares provisional.

@graph.name: ig-ast-measure-real-igs
@graph.title: Measure the AST export on real IGs
@graph.description: Build the WHO SMART Trust and Immunizations IGs through `ig-ast-export` and print the W1/W2 measurements: counts, whether FSH sources sit where the plan expects, and logic-layer edge coverage per resource type against 458 of 458. `--byte-identical` adds a stock build and an `output/` diff.

outputs.name: logic-covered
outputs.description: Logic resources carrying at least one edge to another logic resource in the IG.

@graph.name: ig-ast-pages
@graph.title: Write the IG AST viewer: a page per instance holding `ig-ast` directories, and a hub
@graph.description: For every visualiser an instance declares `renderedBy: ig-ast-pages`, write the hub at `<locale>/<harness>/<id>/` and, with `subgraphs: "instance"`, one page per instance that declares an `ig-ast` directory, at `…/<instance>/`. Each lists the ASTs the directory holds: the IG's package id, resources in total and by type, dependency edges (resolved inside the IG, by origin, by kind), the rebuild plan when one is recorded, and what stays provisional. A declared directory not on disk — a branch-family member not restored, which is the normal case — is reported UNKNOWN with the family it would be restored from, never as zero ASTs. Not `ig-ast-list` extended: that Tool summarises ONE AST it is handed, and a site build has no AST path to hand it.

inputs.name: site
inputs.description: A site being built: the pages go under it (`visualiser-writers.ts` in cat-harness-tools passes it). Absent, they go under the checkout's site directory.

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: The checkout whose declarations are read. Default: the checkout holding the working directory.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when a page is stale, missing or orphaned.

outputs.name: pages
outputs.description: Pages written: the hub and one per instance.

@graph.name: ig-ast-plan
@graph.title: Plan an incremental IG build from a delta of changed files
@graph.description: Map a delta (a commit range, a PR's diff, or the staged index) onto a base AST: which resources to rebuild (the forward cone), which to load from cache, which to remove, or a full build and why. Builds nothing.

install.cli: git clone -b claude/ast-export https://github.com/litlfred/fhir-ig-publisher && cd fhir-ig-publisher/ast-export && mvn -q package && mvn -q dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile=cp.txt

inputs.name: head
inputs.description: Default HEAD; `-staged` diffs the index instead.

inputs.name: fsh-users
inputs.description: `fsh-file-users/v1` from `fsh-cone --file-users`: lets a changed RuleSet- or Alias-only file reach its users rather than force a full build.

outputs.name: rebuild
outputs.description: The forward cone. The plan says `full`, with reasons, when a file's effect cannot be determined or the cone exceeds the threshold.

@graph.name: ig-ast-refresh
@graph.title: Refresh an IG's AST cache on a runner
@graph.description: Dispatch an IG repository's `ig-ast-refresh.yml`, which calls fhir-harness's reusable `.github/workflows/ig-ast-refresh.yml`: mount the layers the IG's index.lock.json pins, restore and judge the cache for `ref`, and when it is not valid (or `force`) run the caller's optional `pre-export` overlay command and build the IG with the pinned Publisher AST exporter (the AST is recorded against the clean commit's inputs, the overlay's changes put back), check the new AST is valid for its commit, and seed `cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/<package id>` with `ig-cache seed --push` — only from a commit on the default branch with the tip's inputs. Builds no site, writes no gh-pages, dispatches nothing.

invoke.shell: gh workflow run ig-ast-refresh.yml --repo <owner/repo> --ref main -f ref=main [-f force=true]

inputs.name: repository
inputs.description: The IG repository that carries the caller (`owner/repo`).

inputs.name: ref
inputs.description: What to build; default `main`. Only a commit on the default branch with the tip's inputs is seeded.

inputs.name: force
inputs.description: Rebuild even when the cache is valid.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: The run's verdict before (`valid`, `stale`, `cannot-tell`, `missing`) and whether it seeded; the AST as a run artifact when it did not.

@graph.name: ig-ast-render
@graph.title: Render a computed IG AST delta as just-the-docs pages
@graph.description: Write the pages for a delta already computed by `ig-ast-diff --json`: an index that lists, a page per changed resource that shows, every one opening with the provisional mark and with Liquid in values neutralised.

inputs.name: delta
inputs.description: `ig-ast-delta/v1`, from `ig-ast-diff --json`.

@graph.name: ig-ast-validity
@graph.title: Is this IG AST still valid for the IG's current inputs?
@graph.description: Run folio-assistant-core's `compiledValidity` on an AST manifest's `inputs`: recompute the input digest (the same algorithm as the Java writer, pinned by a shared golden vector) and the source revision, and answer valid, stale-inputs (naming which input), or cannot-tell.

inputs.name: toolchain
inputs.description: The Publisher that would run now. Without it the toolchain is ASSUMED unchanged, and the result says so.

outputs.name: verdict
outputs.description: Exit 0 valid, 1 stale-inputs, 2 cannot-tell. Cannot-tell is never a pass.

@graph.name: ig-binary-audit
@graph.title: Measure the IG Publisher's binary outputs on a pages branch
@graph.description: Read a pages branch's git tree and report the Publisher's binary outputs (full-ig.zip, package.tgz and variants, package.db, validator packs, the definitions/examples/expansions zips, spreadsheets) by name: copies, bytes, and how much of it sits in branch previews. Reads the tree, never a checkout, so a multi-gigabyte branch costs a depth-1 fetch.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: A clone that has the pages branch fetched.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.description: Default `origin/gh-pages`.

outputs.name: audit
outputs.description: A table, or `ig-binary-audit/v1` JSON with `--json`.

@graph.name: ig-cache
@graph.title: FHIR AST cache
@graph.description: Restore, verify, seed and diagnose the prebuilt AST artefacts for an IG. Always try `restore` first: a full AST build via AstExportCli is expensive, a restore is fast.

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: The verb. `doctor` exists because a restore that silently missed used to look exactly like one that worked.

inputs.name: igRoot
inputs.description: The IG whose AST is acted on.

inputs.name: remote
inputs.description: Git remote to fetch from / push to. Default 'origin'. Use when the IG's origin is upstream (WHO) and the cache lives on a fork.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: A real hit, a miss, or a diagnosis — never a miss that reads as a hit.

@graph.name: ig-pages
@graph.title: Generate an IG instance's reader-facing pages from its artefact index
@graph.description: Write `<instance>/docs/` — an index page, one page per artefact, a page per over-large category and per menu group — from `fhir-artifact-index/index.json` (and `menu.json` when ingested), styled by the template chrome an owning instance ingested. Moved down to this layer because nothing in it was one IG's own (#1767); with `--summary` it writes an instance's landing page, opening with that instance's harness section. For an instance whose docs declare `igSite` (bean `mftp`) it writes no index, menu or category pages — the IG site's own replace them — and only a front-matter `artifacts.md` naming the Tool that drew it. Where an instance declares a visualiser `renderedBy: ig-pages`, it also writes that visualiser's route page, `<base>/<instance>/<id>/`, which opens the artefact index; with `--site <dir>` it writes only those route pages, under that site. For an IG whose SOURCE is at hand, `build-ig-site` renders the IG's own pages instead; this is for an IG known only by what it published.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: The instance directory: holds `fhir-artifact-index/` and receives `docs/`.

inputs.name: site
inputs.description: A site being built: write ONLY the route pages of the visualisers declared `renderedBy: ig-pages` (`<locale>/<harness>/<id>/` and, per instance, `…/<instance>/`) under it, and nothing else: not `docs/`, not the instance. Each opens the IG's artefact index where the site carries it, and is that index otherwise. A repository's own site build passes it (`visualiser-writers.ts` in cat-harness-tools), since the instance is a pinned mount.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: The IG's display name. The index carries only the package id, which stands in when this is absent.

inputs.name: chrome-owner
inputs.description: The instance whose `chrome.json` styles the pages. Absent, the pages are unstyled and the build says so. The banner's identity is always the index's; a chrome ingested from another IG lends its tokens, never its status.

inputs.name: summary
inputs.description: Open the index page with the instance's own declaration (`harness_details.html` with `instance=`), making it the instance's landing page.

inputs.name: full-pages
inputs.description: The opt-out. Without it (the default since 2026-10-12, owner: "make thin default") each artefact page is a THIN shell at the same address: identity and a pointer, the artefact's JSON-LD node beside it, the index node (`artifact/index.jsonld`) the IG site's list pages draw, and one shared renderer, `assets/ig-artifact.js`. With it, the full pages as before, and no JSON-LD. `--thin`, the old opt-in, is accepted and changes nothing.

inputs.name: jsonld-base
inputs.description: Thin pages only: the docs root's published URL, so each node's IRIs are absolute. Absent, they are relative to the node's own file.

inputs.name: compiled-data
inputs.description: Where a compiled index's resource files are served, as a path from the docs root. In an IG site the docs root IS the site root, so it is `ast-data`, not `../ast-data`.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when any page is stale or orphaned.

outputs.name: pages
outputs.description: Pages written; the menu and chrome are reported as present or COULD NOT DETERMINE, never silently absent.

@graph.name: ig-repo-site
@graph.title: Build an IG repository's own site from its cached AST, with no instance declaration
@graph.description: The three checkout scripts the platform's site build runs for a repository that holds an IG and only mounts layers (`index.config.json`): `ig-site:ast` restores the AST from the IG's cache branch (`ig-cache.sh restore`) and judges it, refusing a stale, cannot-tell or absent one (a stale one is accepted for a preview with `SITE_ACCEPT_STALE_AST=1`); `ig-site:compose` derives the artefact index from the AST (binding any IG API sidecars a layer above left in `$SITE_WORK/ig-api/`), writes the thin artefact pages, stages the IG's `input/` and `sushi-config.yaml` (menu read at build time, palette from the webpage theme of the top layer the repository mounts, edit links from its origin) and composes it at the ROOT of the host site source; `ig-site:publisher-pages` serves the AST's resources (`ast-data/` and `<Type>-<id>.json`), the artefact index and the sidecars, refuses a page wearing the IG Publisher's chrome, repairs repeated element ids and stamps `folio-build.json`. Never runs the Publisher and never reads its output. Compose lists the pages it puts in the site in `FOLIO_SITE_UPSTREAM_PAGES`, so the site build reports the IG's own dead links rather than refusing the publish over them.

inputs.name: ig
inputs.description: The IG checkout; the current directory by default.

inputs.name: baseurl
inputs.description: `compose`: the site's base path; `FOLIO_SITE_BASEURL` from the site build when absent.

inputs.name: plantuml-jar
inputs.description: `compose`: render `input/images-source/*.plantuml` as the Publisher does.

inputs.name: work
inputs.description: The site build's work directory (`SITE_WORK` when absent): where `ast` writes its verdict, a layer above leaves the IG API sidecars, and `compose` the index `publisher-pages` serves.

outputs.name: pages
outputs.description: Pages composed, or AST files served.

@graph.name: ig-site-data
@graph.title: Populate site.data.fhir for a just-the-docs IG render
@graph.description: Write the IG Publisher's Jekyll variables (`site.data.fhir.ig.*`, `packageId`, `canonical`) for ONE implementation guide, from `sushi-config.yaml` or a published IG's `fhir-artifact-index`, so pages written for the Publisher render on just-the-docs unchanged. fhir-harness declares `site.data` as a pass-through Liquid prefix; this is what Jekyll then reads (bean `bamf`).

inputs.name: ig
inputs.description: The IG root: holds `sushi-config.yaml`, or `fhir-artifact-index/index.json` for a published IG.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: `<site>/_data/fhir.json` — Jekyll has one `_data/`, so one IG per site, as under the Publisher.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when the file is stale.

outputs.name: written
outputs.description: Fields written, each from a named source.

outputs.name: undetermined
outputs.description: Fields a Publisher build would have that no source here carries. LISTED, never written as empty strings, because Jekyll prints an empty string and an absent value identically.

@graph.name: ingest-ig-menu
@graph.title: Ingest an IG's navigation from its sushi-config
@graph.description: Read `menu:` (and the page tree) out of an IG source repository's `sushi-config.yaml` into `fhir-artifact-index/menu.json`, recording the repository and commit it was read at — the declared source `stage-ig-sites` clones. `--check` re-derives it against a checkout; with no `--source` it reports COULD NOT DETERMINE and exits 2, never 0.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: A checkout of the IG source repository.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: The instance's `fhir-artifact-index/` directory.

inputs.name: check
inputs.description: Write nothing; exit 1 when stale, 2 when it cannot compare.

outputs.name: groups
outputs.description: Menu groups read, each with its items.

@graph.name: ingest-ig-releases
@graph.title: Record an IG's GitHub releases as pointers to their binary assets
@graph.description: Read an IG repository's GitHub releases and write `fhir-artifact-index/releases.json` (`ig-releases/v1`): each asset's name, size, SHA-256 digest and download URL, never its bytes. The IG site's generated `releases` page lists them (bean `b8ip`).

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: `owner/repo`; default the instance menu's recorded IG source, else its declaration's `repository`.

outputs.name: releases
outputs.description: `<instance>/fhir-artifact-index/releases.json`.

@graph.name: jsonld-vocabularies
@graph.title: ValueSet expansions → JSON-LD
@graph.description: JSON-LD vocabularies built from the ValueSet expansions in the published output.

inputs.name: ast
inputs.description: The IG's AST (`output-ast/`, with the build's `expansions.json`).

outputs.name: vocabularies
outputs.description: `*.jsonld` at the published root.

@graph.name: logical-model-schemas
@graph.title: Logical models → JSON Schema
@graph.description: A JSON Schema per logical model, from the published FHIR resources.

inputs.name: ast
inputs.description: The IG's AST (`output-ast/`, with the build's `expansions.json`).

outputs.name: logicalModelSchemas
outputs.description: `schemas/<stem>.schema.json`, one per logical model.

@graph.name: pin-ig-terminology
@graph.title: Snapshot a published IG's terminology at its pinned version
@graph.description: Read every CodeSystem concept out of a FHIR IG clone checked out at its pinned tag and write a `folio-pinned-terminology/v1` snapshot: the offline, version-fixed answer `check:term-mapping` resolves its `fhir` target against. Which IG, which pin record and which snapshot path are the caller's (`--pin`, `--out`, `--source`); this layer names none (#1767, stage B′).

inputs.name: from
inputs.description: A clone of the IG checked out at the PINNED tag, passed as `--from`. The script refuses unless that clone's `sushi-config.yaml` version equals the pin's, so a newer clone cannot silently become the snapshot.

outputs.name: snapshot
outputs.description: The `--out` path, `folio-pinned-terminology/v1`: the version, the source, and every `system#code` with its display, sorted.

@graph.name: sdc-checks
@graph.title: Check an IG's built Questionnaires with CSIRO's SDC libraries
@graph.description: Build-time Structured Data Capture checks, one result per Questionnaire (`sdcChecks[]` of `fhir-questionnaire-wireframe`): `assemble` (`@aehrc/sdc-assemble` 2.0.3: an assemble-root's sub-forms resolve in this IG, and `--out` writes the assembled Questionnaire), `template-extract` (`@aehrc/sdc-template-extract` 1.0.16: extraction from the IG's fixture response yields the expected resources), `populate` (`@aehrc/sdc-populate` 4.7.2: FHIRPath pre-population from a fixture context gives the expected answers) and `behaviour` (`@aehrc/questionnaire-test-toolkit` 0.1.0: the IG's own behavioural test, warn-only). Owner, 2026-10-14: checks, not UI.

inputs.name: ast
inputs.description: The IG's FHIR AST (`output-ast/`): its Questionnaires, and the canonicals a sub-form resolves against.

inputs.name: questionnaire
inputs.description: A Questionnaire id to check; default every one in the AST.

inputs.name: fixtures
inputs.description: One directory per Questionnaire id: `response.json` + `extract-expected.json`, `populate-context.json` + `populate-expected.json`, `behaviour.test.tsx`.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where assembled Questionnaires are written.

outputs.name: sdcChecks
outputs.description: Per Questionnaire, per check: pass, fail, not-applicable, no-fixture or could-not-determine — the last three never a pass. JSON with `--json`. Exit 1 on an error-severity failure; behavioural tests never fail the run.

@graph.name: stage-ig-sites
@graph.title: Stage every IG whose instance records its source, one Jekyll site each
@graph.description: For every instance holding `fhir-artifact-index/menu.json` with a sushi-config source, clone the IG at the recorded commit and stage it with `build-ig-site`: the instance's webpage theme (inherited along `needs` when it declares none), its artefact pages and `artifacts` page, its post-processing fills, and an edit link to the IG's default branch. An instance whose docs directory declares `igSite` is staged to be served AT `/<instance>/` with its artefact pages copied in (a collision is refused); otherwise beside it at `/<instance>/ig/`. Prints one `<instance> <jekyll source> <at>` line per IG for the caller's `jekyll build` (beans `bamf`, `mftp`).

inputs.name: work
inputs.description: Scratch directory: each IG's clone and its Jekyll source.

inputs.name: baseurl
inputs.description: The site's base URL; each IG is served under it at `/<instance>/` or `/<instance>/ig/`.

inputs.name: plantuml-jar
inputs.description: Render `input/images-source/*.plantuml` as the Publisher does.

inputs.name: changed-files
inputs.description: Build only the IGs a changed file reaches (the staging cone, bean `4j86`).

inputs.name: compose-into
inputs.description: Move each staged IG into this host Jekyll source at `<instance>/`, so the host's build renders it: in the thin layout with the host's rail linked (the default), or with the host's full chrome (sidebar, search, language selector) under `--full-pages`.

inputs.name: compose-at-root
inputs.description: With `--compose-into` and `--only`: the IG IS the site — compose it at the host's ROOT, based at `--baseurl` itself. An IG repository's own site uses this with a `compose-docs --shell` host, so it wears the main site's chrome (#2235).

inputs.name: only
inputs.description: Build one IG instance.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: With `--only`: a local checkout of the IG's source to build from instead of cloning the recorded commit — an IG repository building its own site in CI.

inputs.name: full-pages
inputs.description: The opt-out. Without it (the default since 2026-10-12, owner: "make thin default") `artifacts.html` and `toc.html` are thin pages over the artefact index node, and composed IG pages wear the thin layout with the host's chrome linked, not inlined. With it, the full pages as before; it needs `gen-ig-pages --full-pages` too, and a mismatch is refused.

outputs.name: sites
outputs.description: IGs staged, one stdout line each; an instance with no recorded source is skipped and reported, never silently.

@graph.name: strip-library-binaries
@graph.title: Strip binary payloads from Library resources
@graph.description: Remove base64 `content.data` from published `Library` resources, so an IG embedding compiled CQL does not ship the bytes twice.

inputs.name: igOutput
inputs.description: The Publisher's `output/`. It runs AFTER the build — the resources it edits are published ones.

outputs.name: stripped
outputs.description: How many resources were altered. Zero is a determined empty when the output directory was found; a missing output directory is a different state.

@graph.name: strip-library-content
@graph.title: Replace inline Library content with URL references
@graph.description: Replace inline CQL/ELM in `Library` resources with a URL reference to the published copy.

outputs.name: references
outputs.description: The base the replacement references resolve against. If it is wrong, every rewritten Library points at nothing and the resource still validates.

@graph.name: terminology-index
@graph.title: Write an IG site's static terminology index from the IG's own cache
@graph.description: Read the IG Publisher's `expansions.json` and `txcache/`, as `ig-cache.sh restore` leaves them, and write `index.json` (gzipped as `index.json.gz` over 1 MB): every code with its system and display, and each value set's codes. The IG site's service worker answers the self-hosted Form Builder's LOINC search from it, and its UCUM search from the vendored full UCUM list, so the site makes no cross-site call (owner, 2026-10-14: "cache + ucum. this is gh-pages so no XSS"). `build-ig-site` runs it for every IG with a Questionnaire.

inputs.name: expansions
inputs.description: `output-ast/expansions.json`.

inputs.name: txcache
inputs.description: `input-cache/txcache/`.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Where `index.json` (or `index.json.gz`) is written.

outputs.name: index
outputs.description: The index file, and a count of codes and value sets on stdout.

@graph.name: valueset-schemas
@graph.title: ValueSets → JSON Schema
@graph.description: A JSON Schema per ValueSet, plus the enumeration-response schemas published at the IG root.

inputs.name: ast
inputs.description: The IG's AST (`output-ast/`, with the build's `expansions.json`).

outputs.name: valueSetSchemas
outputs.description: One schema per ValueSet, plus the enumeration-response schemas at the IG root.
